ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows trapezoid FGJK, with the upper base FG labeled x, and the lower base KJ labeled 18.2. The middle horizontal segment LH is labeled 15. The tick marks on the left and right legs respectively indicate that L and H are the midpoints of the two legs, so LH is the midline of the trapezoid. Reasoning: The length of the midline of a trapezoid is equal to the average of the lengths of the two bases, so 15 = (x + 18.2) / 2. method.method_draft: Read the figure first: the top horizontal base FG has length x, the bottom horizontal base KJ has length 18.2, and LH, drawn through midpoint marks on both legs, has length 15. Instead of invoking the theorem as a memorized formula, model the trapezoid with coordinates: place the bottom base endpoints at horizontal coordinates 0 and 18.2, and place the top base endpoints so their horizontal separation is x. Since L and H are midpoints of the two nonparallel sides, their horizontal coordinates are the averages of the corresponding endpoint coordinates, making LH's length the average of the two base lengths. Thus 15 = (x + 18.2)/2, then solve for x.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The attached diagram shows trapezoid FGJK. The top horizontal base FG is labeled x, the bottom horizontal base KJ is labeled 18.2, and the horizontal segment LH inside the trapezoid is labeled 15. Tick marks on the left leg FK show FL and LK are congruent, and tick marks on the right leg GJ show GH and HJ are congruent, so L and H are midpoints of the legs.

Reasoning: Model the trapezoid with coordinates. Put the bottom base endpoints at K = 0 and J = 18.2 horizontally. Let the top base endpoints have horizontal coordinates a and a + x, so FG has length x. Since L is the midpoint of FK, its horizontal coordinate is the average of the horizontal coordinates of F and K: a/2. Since H is the midpoint of GJ, its horizontal coordinate is the average of the horizontal coordinates of G and J: (a + x + 18.2)/2. Therefore the length LH is ((a + x + 18.2)/2) - (a/2) = (x + 18.2)/2. The diagram gives LH = 15, so 15 = (x + 18.2)/2. Then 30 = x + 18.2, so x = 11.8.
